title: Why I Stayed at the Firm
content: Almost thirty years at the same company. People ask me why. [pause] I came from a state pension board. Important work, but... distant from real people. At the firm, I saw something different. The whole place was built on a crazy idea: what if a fund company acted like it worked for the people whose money it held? What if we weren't trying to maximize profits but minimize costs? [pause] I remember thinking: this is either genius or insane. Turns out it was both. [laughter] [pause] But honestly? I stayed because of the mission. Every basis point we shaved off fees was money in someone's retirement. Every family that reached their goals because we kept things simple... that's real. That matters. [pause] I could have made more money elsewhere. But I don't know if I could have made more meaning.
follow_up: Walt used to say: 'Every dollar we don't charge is a dollar that stays in somebody's kitchen.' That still gives me goosebumps.
lesson: Find work that aligns with your values. The money follows meaning more than meaning follows money.
